title: Cancel the extra cut to Civil Service running costs
noun: cancelling the extra Civil Service cut
headline: Cancel the extra admin cut. Costs £0.6bn in 2029-30.
description: Departments’ administration budgets are cut by 20% by 2029-30 instead of the 16% the Spending Review planned, saving £0.6 billion a year by then. Switch this on to cancel the extra cut and give that money back.

baselinePolicy.text: Departmental administration budgets fall by 20% by 2029-30, against 16% in the Spending Review 2025 plans (Table 6.1 line 63).

source.quote: the government is going further by reducing departmental administration budgets by 20% by 2029‑30

alreadyIncludes: Departmental administration budgets fall by 20% by 2029-30, against 16% in the Spending Review 2025 plans (Table 6.1 line 63).

lines.title: Future Civil Service: Reduce administration budgets by 20% by 2029-30 compared to 16% reduction in Spending Review 2025 plans

rawSource.note: Reversal on the spending side: the Treasury’s costing with the sign kept (a line that reduced borrowing is spending the reversal adds back; a line that cost money is spending the reversal saves).

caveats: The Treasury’s costing is on the OBR October 2026 forecast, the baseline used here. Effects before the start year are not applied: 2026-27 falls before any Budget of yours.
The OBR already doubts that every planned efficiency saving arrives; cancelling this one puts the money back in the plans, not in any particular service.

considerations.text: The Treasury’s scorecard figure is the Budget’s own costing of the measure, certified by the OBR as part of its October 2026 forecast.
